sentences.text: Henry III -LRB- 1 October 1207 -- 16 November 1272 -RRB- , also known as Henry of Winchester , was King of England , Lord of Ireland and Duke of Aquitaine from 1216 until his death .	King of England	King of England	Lord of Ireland	Lordship of Ireland	Duke of Aquitaine	Duke of Aquitaine

The son of King John and Isabella of Angoulême , Henry assumed the throne when he was only nine in the middle of the First Barons ' War .	John	John, King of England	King John	John, King of England	Isabella of Angoulême	Isabella of Angoulême

Cardinal Guala declared the war against the rebel barons to be a religious crusade and Henry 's forces , led by William Marshal , defeated the rebels at the battles of Lincoln and Sandwich in 1217 .	Guala	Guala Bicchieri	William Marshal	William Marshal, 1st Earl of Pembroke	Lincoln	Battle of Lincoln (1217)	Sandwich	Battle of Sandwich (1217)	crusade	crusade
Henry promised to abide by the Great Charter of 1225 , which limited royal power and protected the rights of the major barons .	Great Charter of 1225	Magna Carta#The Great Charter 1225

His early rule was dominated first by Hubert de Burgh and then Peter des Roches , who re-established royal authority after the war .	Hubert de Burgh	Hubert de Burgh, 1st Earl of Kent	Peter des Roches	Peter des Roches

In 1230 the King attempted to reconquer the provinces of France that had once belonged to his father , but the invasion was a debacle .	provinces of France	John, King of England#Loss of Normandy, 1202–04

A revolt led by William Marshal 's son , Richard , broke out in 1232 , ending in a peace settlement negotiated by the Church .	William Marshal	William Marshal, 1st Earl of Pembroke	Richard	Richard, 1st Earl of Cornwall	the Church	Christianity in England
Following the revolt , Henry ruled England personally , rather than governing through senior ministers .
He travelled less than previous monarchs , investing heavily in a handful of his favourite palaces and castles .	palaces and castles	Castles in Great Britain and Ireland#Palace-fortresses
He married Eleanor of Provence , with whom he had five children .	Eleanor of Provence	Eleanor of Provence

Henry was known for his piety , holding lavish religious ceremonies and giving generously to charities ; the King was particularly devoted to the figure of Edward the Confessor , whom he adopted as his patron saint .	piety	piety	Edward the Confessor	Edward the Confessor	patron saint	patron saint	Edward	Edward I of England

He extracted huge sums of money from the Jews in England , ultimately crippling their ability to do business , and as attitudes towards the Jews hardened , he introduced the Statute of Jewry , attempting to segregate the community .	Jews in England	History of the Jews in England	Statute of Jewry	Statute of Jewry

In a fresh attempt to reclaim his family 's lands in France , he invaded Poitou in 1242 , leading to the disastrous Battle of Taillebourg .	invaded Poitou	Saintonge War	Battle of Taillebourg	Battle of Taillebourg
After this , Henry relied on diplomacy , cultivating an alliance with Holy Roman Emperor Frederick II .	Holy Roman Emperor Frederick II	Frederick II, Holy Roman Emperor

Henry supported his brother Richard in his bid to become King of the Romans in 1256 , but was unable to place his own son Edmund on the throne of Sicily , despite investing large amounts of money .	Richard	Richard, 1st Earl of Cornwall	King of the Romans	King of the Romans	Edmund	Edmund Crouchback	Sicily	Kingdom of Sicily
He planned to go on crusade to the Levant , but was prevented from doing so by rebellions in Gascony .	crusade	crusade	Levant	Levant	Gascony	Gascony

By 1258 , Henry 's rule was increasingly unpopular , the result of the failure of his expensive foreign policies and the notoriety of his Poitevin half-brothers , the Lusignans , as well as the role of his local officials in collecting taxes and debts .	Poitevin	Poitiers	Lusignans	Lusignan dynasty

A coalition of his barons , initially probably backed by Eleanor , seized power in a coup d'état and expelled the Poitevins from England , reforming the royal government through a process called the Provisions of Oxford .	Provisions of Oxford	Provisions of Oxford

Henry and the baronial government enacted a peace with France in 1259 , under which Henry gave up his rights to his other lands in France in return for King Louis IX of France recognising him as the rightful ruler of Gascony .	Gascony	Gascony	peace with France	Treaty of Paris (1259)	King Louis IX of France	Louis IX of France
The baronial regime collapsed but Henry was unable to reform a stable government and instability across England continued .
In 1263 one of the more radical barons , Simon de Montfort , seized power , resulting in the Second Barons ' War .	Simon de Montfort	Simon de Montfort, 6th Earl of Leicester
Henry persuaded Louis to support his cause and mobilised an army .
The Battle of Lewes occurred in 1264 , where Henry was defeated and taken prisoner .	Battle of Lewes	Battle of Lewes

Henry 's eldest son , Edward , escaped from captivity to defeat de Montfort at the Battle of Evesham the following year and freed his father .	Edward	Edward I of England	Battle of Evesham	Battle of Evesham

Henry initially enacted a harsh revenge on the remaining rebels , but was persuaded by the Church to mollify his policies through the Dictum of Kenilworth .	the Church	Christianity in England	Dictum of Kenilworth	Dictum of Kenilworth
Reconstruction was slow and Henry had to acquiesce to various measures , including further suppression of the Jews , to maintain baronial and popular support .
Henry died in 1272 , leaving Edward as his successor .	Edward	Edward I of England
He was buried in Westminster Abbey , which he had rebuilt in the second half of his reign , and was moved to his current tomb in 1290 .	Westminster Abbey	Westminster Abbey	Westminster	Westminster
Some miracles were declared after his death but he was not canonised .	canonised	Canonization
